The position remains commercially connected, working closely with operational leaders to interpret performance, understand cost and margin drivers, and support sound business decisions. You’ll join a well-established, values-led organisation with a practical, collaborative culture and a sizeable operational footprint. The business has the moving parts and performance drivers typically associated with a complex production environment.

  • CA qualified or equivalent preferred, although strong experience gained in a broad, senior accounting position will also be considered.
  • At least five years’ finance experience, with sound exposure to financial and management accounting, month-end ownership, budgeting, forecasting and cashflow.

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
The Opportunity
This is Evnex’s first dedicated Finance Business Partner role. The finance team has built the foundations: actuals reported as an integrated three-statement set, a 13-week cash flow forecast, and a new 12-month rolling forecast model being implemented now. Your job is to pick that work up, own it in detail, and take it to the next level.
  
You will report to the senior finance manager and work closely with the CFO on the forecast model, the annual budget, and the quarterly board pack. You will also partner with leaders across the business, turning financial analysis into decisions and following through on the actions agreed. The finance function is striving for global best practice for a business of its size, and AI tools are part of how the work gets done every day.
  
This is a step-up role for someone who has already done the work and now wants ownership of it. In your first two weeks you will build your own 90-day plan, and there is a clear path to grow as Evnex and its finance team scale.
  
The Company
Founded in Christchurch, Evnex designs and manufactures smart EV chargers for homes and businesses across New Zealand and Australia, including the Evnex E2 range and the X-series. More than 20,000 Evnex chargers are now installed across the two countries. Its mission is to make electrification effortless, and the clean energy transition is the reason the company exists.
  
Evnex is a Series A, private equity backed company. The business is growing, holds significant inventory, and reports quarterly to its board and investors. It is a small team solving a hard problem, where most people do more than their title suggests and everyone is expected to own their work.
  
The Role
  • Take ownership of the new forecast model and run it as an integrated three-statement, 12-month rolling forecast, working closely with the CFO on its development and build-out
  • Run the annual budget with the CFO, and the monthly to quarterly reforecast and variance analysis, with commentary for the leadership team
  • Work alongside the CFO in preparing the quarterly board pack
  • Run the weekly 13-week cash flow forecast cycle and variance analysis with the senior finance manager
  • Partner with department leads on detailed financial analysis that drives business improvement
  • Improve models and data flows from Business Central and HubSpot, using AI and automation to reduce manual work
  • Support the senior finance manager with month-end analysis, a small and capped part of the role
  
Your Profile
  • CA or CPA qualified, or close to it, with at least three years’ finance experience
  • Hands-on experience doing forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis yourself, not only reviewing it
  • A working understanding of how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement link
  • Strong Excel and financial modelling skills, with models others can follow
  • Able to explain financial concepts to non-finance people in plain English
  • Curious about AI tools and keen to use them as a core part of the work
  • Experience in a manufacturing, distribution, or inventory-intensive business is desirable but not essential
  • Unrestricted working rights in New Zealand. Evnex is unable to offer sponsorship.
  
Evnex has partnered exclusively with Profile Group to recruit this Finance Business Partner position. If you are interested in hearing more about this role, please call Louis Bentley on 022 4269 569, Tim Best on 021 502 791 or apply below.

job.title: Commercial Accountant
job.description:
Louis-pbentley The Opportunity
This is a broad commercial seat, not a narrow ledger role. A Christchurch expe business needs someone who can sit with operations, build the numbers behind each project, and still roll their sleeves up when the finance team is short.
You will model pricing across programmes, build detailed budgets with the operational staff who used to own that work, and look at margins with the people who can actually change them. Alongside that sits a live systems project: due diligence and support on a new ERP, plus room to use AI where it makes dashboards and analysis faster.

Month-end is shared, not owned end to end. You will help the team hit a working-day-ten close, support wash-ups, and step in on year-end IFRS reporting when it is needed. The rest of the week is commercial: fees, surcharges, stakeholder questions, and the odd transactional job that keeps the Financial Accountant and Management Accountant moving.
If you like a mixed bag, and you would rather improve a process than protect one, this is that role. The business name stays confidential until you are ready to talk.

The Company
A small team with global footprint. You will work with operational staff, the Financial Accountant and the Management Accountant. Personality matters here. The useful version of this role is curious, plain-spoken, and comfortable switching between a pricing model and a cutoff.
The Role A usual stretch of work looks like this:
  • Model pricing for programmes and test how changes land on yield and margin.
  • Build detailed budgets with operational staff, as that work moves into accounts.
  • Partner on margin analysis, and work through payment fees and surcharge settings with the right stakeholders.
  • Support due diligence and implementation of a new ERP, including how trip, commercial and finance data should connect.
  • Help the team hit the working-day-ten close, including wash-ups and occasional month-end support.
  • Support year-end IFRS reporting, and pick up transactional work for the Financial Accountant and Management Accountant.
  • Use AI and modern tools to build dashboards and shorten analysis the team currently does by hand.
  • Various more transactional work to support the wider team when required
Your Profile
You will bring:
  • A background in management or commercial accounting, with real time in budgeting, pricing or margin work. A degree or progress towards CA is useful, not a gate.
  • Comfort with systems. You can hold your own in an ERP review, and you like fixing how data moves, not only how a spreadsheet looks.
  • A digital habit. You already use AI, or you are keen to, for dashboards, analysis and the repetitive parts of finance.
  • Sound interpersonal skills. Operations will only hand over budgets if they trust the person asking the questions.
  • An analytical eye and a practical streak. You can support a close on working day ten and still come back to the commercial question afterwards.
How to Apply

If this sounds like the next step you have been looking for, we would like to hear from you. Apply via the relevant link or reach out for a confidential conversation: Louis | louis@profilegroup.co.nz | 0224 269 569.

job.title: Systems Accountant
job.description:
About Apollo Projects
Apollo Projects is a nationwide design and build construction company delivering complex, high-quality projects across New Zealand. For more than 25 years, the business has built a strong reputation not only for the projects it delivers, but for the way its people work together to get them done.

At the heart of Apollo is a down-to-earth, collaborative culture. They look for good people who are passionate about what they do, curious enough to ask questions, willing to challenge thinking and keen to find better ways of doing things. People who enjoy working as part of a team, take ownership, bring a positive mindset and don’t take themselves too seriously tend to feel at home there.

Relationships have always mattered at Apollo. Whether it’s with clients, consultants, subcontractors or each other, the focus is on building trust, doing what they say they’ll do and working through challenges together. Their values, including “own it, solve it”, a glass-half-full mindset and having fun along the way, are reflected in how the business operates day to day.

That people-first approach extends beyond Apollo’s own team. The business is committed to creating a positive impact in the communities it works in, supporting initiatives across youth sport, water safety, helping families in need and community projects throughout New Zealand.

Apollo Benefits
Apollo puts real focus on creating a workplace where people feel supported, valued and able to do their best work. Alongside a collaborative culture and plenty of opportunity to grow, employees have access to a range of benefits designed to support wellbeing, development and life outside of work.
  • Competitive salary reflective of skills and experience
  • Southern Cross Health Insurance, with discounted cover available for immediate family
  • Wellbeing support including EAP, free flu vaccinations and access to the My Everyday Wellbeing platform
  • WorkRide, providing access to a bike, e-bike or e-scooter through a pre-tax salary sacrifice scheme
  • Ongoing training and development, including work with Te Pūheke to strengthen understanding of Te Ao Māori across the business
  • Free company accommodation in Blenheim for personal use
  • Genuine access to Apollo’s founders, who remain actively involved in the business after 25 years
  • A team that genuinely values giving back and sees community involvement as part of how the business operates

The Opportunity
This is a broad Systems Accountant role sitting at the intersection of finance, systems and data.

Working closely with Finance, Quantity Surveying and operational teams, you’ll play an important role in ensuring Apollo’s financial systems, reporting and data remain accurate, reliable and useful for the people making decisions across the business.

You’ll take ownership of Jobpac and related finance and reporting platforms, becoming a key internal point of contact for system improvements, reporting and process changes. You’ll also help lead the development of a data warehouse environment, bringing financial and operational information together in a way that gives the business better visibility.

There is plenty of scope to make the role your own. You’ll build and maintain Power BI reporting, improve processes, support system changes, while contributing to projects that make information easier to access and use.

Alongside the systems focus, you’ll remain closely connected to the wider Finance function, supporting month-end and year-end processes, management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, audit, tax and statutory compliance.

It’s a role that would suit someone who likes to understand how things work, spot where something could be better and then follow it through.

The Role
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Owning and supporting Apollo’s finance systems, including Jobpac, related applications, integrations and reporting tools
  • Leading the development, implementation and ongoing maintenance of a data warehouse solution for financial and operational data
  • Developing and maintaining Jobpac reporting, Power BI dashboards and other business intelligence reporting
  • Turning data into meaningful analysis and insights that support decision-making across the business
  • Identifying opportunities to improve systems, processes and reporting efficiency
  • Supporting system upgrades, testing, integrations, data migration and change initiatives
  • Assisting the wider Finance team with month-end and year-end reporting, statutory compliance, budgeting, forecasting and cash flow reporting
  • Supporting tax, audit and other recurring finance requirements
  • Contributing to wider finance and business improvement projects as required

Your Profile
You’ll likely bring a mix of accounting knowledge and systems capability, along with a natural interest in how things can be improved.

You won’t be expected to know everything on day one, but you’ll be someone who is comfortable getting into the detail and asking the right questions. You’ll also be able to work across different parts of the business and explain technical or financial information in a way that makes sense.

Ideally, you’ll have:
  • A degree in accounting, finance or a related discipline
  • Experience working with ERP systems, including reporting, configuration, testing or process improvement
  • Strong Power BI capability, including DAX and Power Query, along with advanced Excel skills
  • A solid understanding of accounting processes, financial controls, month-end
  • The ability to explain technical or financial information clearly to different audiences
  • Experience with system integrations, data migration, UAT or change implementation
  • Exposure to data warehouse design, ETL or data quality would be advantageous
  • Jobpac or another construction or project-based ERP system would be useful, but is not essential
  • Experience within construction, contracting or another project-based environment would be beneficial
  • CA or equivalent would be an advantage, but is not essential

Just as importantly, Apollo is looking for someone who cares about doing a good job and enjoys working with others. Someone who is happy to ask questions, take responsibility and get stuck in when something needs improving.

Apollo Projects have partnered exclusively with Profile Group to recruit this position. If you’re interested in hearing more about this role, please contact Tim Best on 021 502 791, Louis Bentley on 022 4269 569, or apply below.
